findings.title: マクドナルド公式アプリのデータベースへの不正アクセスに関するお知らせとお詫び
findings.summary_md: Japan McDonald's said a third party accessed part of the customer-related data in the database for its official mobile app. The listed fields are product purchase histories, an internal customer-management ID, IP addresses and location from mobile devices used when the service was provided; names, email addresses, phone numbers, addresses and card details were not included. The company said it had not confirmed any unauthorized use of the app or services, was invalidating the authentication credentials used in the access, investigating related systems and reporting to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission. It said it would update the notice as new information became available.

findings.title: マクドナルド公式アプリ 不正アクセス 購入履歴・位置情報 | ITD
findings.summary_md: ITD published a first report on November 23, 2026, based on the company's notice. It listed purchase histories, the internal customer-management ID, IP addresses and device location as affected, and noted that names, email, phone numbers, addresses and payment card data were not. The article flagged the victim count, intrusion route, timing, whether data left the systems and individual notification as unanswered, and advised users to review app location permissions and check their order history.

findings.title: ASCII.jp：マクドナルド公式アプリに不正アクセス　購入履歴やスマホの位置情報が対象に
findings.summary_md: ASCII reported on November 24, 2026 that McDonald's Japan had disclosed third-party access to part of the customer data in its official app database on November 20. It repeated the four affected fields and the exclusion of names, email addresses, phone numbers, addresses and card data, and said the company found no unauthorized app or service use. The company was invalidating the authentication credentials used in the access, investigating related systems and reporting to Japan's data protection authority, with further updates promised.

findings.title: マクドナルド公式アプリに不正アクセス - CNET Japan
findings.summary_md: CNET Japan reported on November 24, 2026 that McDonald's Japan disclosed unauthorized third-party access to its official app database on November 20. The article listed purchase histories, IP addresses, an internal customer-management ID and device location, and said names, email addresses, phone numbers, addresses and credit card data were not included. It noted that the company had not said how many users were affected or whether data was exfiltrated, and was invalidating the credentials used in the intrusion while reporting to Japan's data protection authority.
